q: What does branch and bound use that plain backtracking does not?
options: A bound on the best value reachable below each node, compared with the best solution so far
explain: Both use a state space tree and feasibility tests. Branch and bound also prunes nodes that cannot beat the current best.

q: For a maximisation knapsack, which bound is used at a node?
options: Value so far plus the fractional-knapsack value of the remaining items
Sum of all remaining values, ignoring weight
explain: The fractional value is an upper bound: allowing fractions can only help. Ignoring weight entirely would also be an upper bound, but a much weaker one.

q: Which data structure holds the live nodes in least-cost (LC) branch and bound?
explain: LC always expands the live node with the best bound. A queue gives FIFO branch and bound, and a stack behaves like backtracking.

q: W = 10. Items (weight, value) in ratio order: (3, 30), (4, 32), (5, 35), (6, 30). What is the root's upper bound?
explain: Take items 1 and 2 (weight 7, value 62), then 3/5 of item 3: 62 + 21 = 83.

q: A live node has upper bound 64 and the best complete solution found so far is 65. What happens to it?
options: It is moved to the back of the queue
explain: Nothing below it can reach more than 64, which is less than 65.

q: Branch and bound guarantees a polynomial running time for the 0/1 knapsack problem.
explain: False. In the worst case it may still explore an exponential number of nodes.

q: Why must items be sorted by value/weight before computing the fractional bound?
options: Otherwise the bound can be too small and wrongly prune the optimum
To find the answer in O(n)
explain: The fractional optimum fills the capacity in ratio order. Any other order may give a value below the true fractional optimum, which is then not a valid upper bound.

q: When a 'take item i' child is feasible, its value so far is a valid solution and may update the best.
explain: True. Leaving all later items out is always allowed, so any feasible partial selection is a complete solution.

q: What is the main advantage of branch and bound over the DP of topic 27 for 0/1 knapsack?
options: Its running time does not grow with the capacity W
explain: The DP is Θ(n·W), which is hopeless for huge W. Branch and bound depends on how well it prunes, not on the size of W.

q: FIFO branch and bound explores the state space tree in which order?
explain: A queue processes nodes in the order they were generated, one level at a time.
